claim: A watch-over service from the 15-min meter profile alerted a relative in 12 h (simulated).
limit: Simulated only; no real household, no clinical or legal validation, not an emergency device.
alt: A week of simulated 15-minute household load with a shaded usual range. On the last day nothing rises above the range after the evening stop, a check-in message goes out, and the relative is notified later that morning.
post:
Many older people live alone, and the first sign that something is wrong is often silence: no kettle, no cooker, no lights in the morning. Swiss utilities are rolling out smart meters that record the household load every 15 minutes, with a legal target of 80 percent of metering points by the end of 2027. Japanese electricity utilities already use such meter data for watch-over services.

I built an open-source, opt-in version: it learns each household's routine from the 15-minute profile only (no camera, no wearable), notices unusual inactivity, sends a gentle check-in to the person first and then notifies a relative, with a plain-text reason such as 'no household activity by 11:05; usually by 08:10'. Only derived daily-routine features leave the home.

Measured on simulated households (5 personas, falls, night events, hospital stays): 88% of stops alerted within 24 h, median 12.0 h to the relative. False relative alerts: 1.5 per household-year if 9 in 10 check-ins are answered, 14.2 if nobody ever answers. A 2 kW heat pump cut detection to 42% (no heat pump: 88%); 1-minute data reached 78% and 60-minute data 10%.

Not verified: any real household, real meter data latency, real replies to SMS, legal review. It is not a medical or emergency device.

Would you opt in for a parent, and what would you need to see first?

Code: https://github.com/VB-Builds/meter-wellbeing-watch
